brief:
WHAT HAPPENED
- Paramount completed a $110bn merger with Warner Bros following months of legal challenges and competition concerns.
- BT reached an agreement on a rescue deal to buy broadband operator TalkTalk, which remains subject to regulatory approval.
- Energy company Equinor warned it may avoid future UK investments if oil and gas fields at Rosebank and Jackdaw are not approved.
- The UK average five-year fixed mortgage rate reached 6% for the first time in three years as lenders face increased costs.
- The Pentagon stopped using Anthropic AI tools after blacklisting the firm as a supply chain risk over safety guardrail disputes.

WHY IT MATTERS
- A corporate merger—the combining of two existing businesses into one entity—at this scale reshapes the media and entertainment industry landscape.
- A fixed mortgage rate is an interest rate locked in for a set period; hitting 6% means home loans have become more expensive for borrowers seeking long-term rate certainty.
- Equinor's warning links regulatory project approvals directly to corporate willingness to commit capital expenditure in the energy sector.

WHAT TO WATCH TODAY
- Regulatory evaluation and required approvals concerning BT's proposed takeover of TalkTalk.
- Government decisions and formal responses regarding the Rosebank and Jackdaw field applications.
- Continued industry developments surrounding the US military's cessation of Anthropic AI tools.
- Public and market reactions to rising UK mortgage rates crossing the 6% threshold.

IN SIMPLE TERMS
Major corporate consolidations and rising borrowing costs are dominating the news. Paramount has completed a massive $110bn takeover of Warner Bros, and BT has agreed to purchase TalkTalk pending approval. Meanwhile, average UK five-year mortgage rates have hit 6%, energy giant Equinor is questioning future UK energy investments over project approvals, and the US military has stopped using Anthropic's AI software.
